item: A start that cannot make its worker thread no longer leaves a running job with no worker
summary: Thread.start() raises RuntimeError (can't start new thread) when the process or machine is out of threads; the volume-backup manager, the import queue, the folder backup and the search re-index had already set their job to running (the queue and the re-index also saved it) and called start() with nothing around it. The Task Manager then listed a running job with a Pause and a Cancel that acted on nothing, and the volume manager and the import queue refused every later start for the life of the process (the next start joined a thread that was never started and raised). Each now takes an Exception from start(): the volume manager and the folder backup say error with the exception class only, the import queue puts back the run it had and drops the passphrase, the search re-index saves error; the error still reaches the caller. 8 tests, all red on the old code. Exception only (R393); stated limits in the lesson.
